title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten settings for solo reading, group work, computer tasks, reflection, and hands-on projects—with access and reservation limits attached.

cards.title: Spread Out in Edwards Atrium
cards.subtitle: A sunny Anderson Hall setting designed for group projects
cards.notes: Bring collaborative work here when Anderson Hall is open; check the room-request link before planning an organized or exclusive session.
cards.short_summary: A bright atrium suited to project teams that need shared table space.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus identifies Edwards Atrium as a sunny study location and says Anderson Hall’s main-level atrium is used for group projects and events.
cards.access_notes: Building access follows campus schedules; events or reservations may supersede informal use.

cards.title: Take a Seat Upstairs in Anderson
cards.subtitle: A student lounge near the education library and digital classroom
cards.notes: Use the lounge for reading or low-key collaboration, but leave the neighboring classroom and education library to their posted uses.
cards.short_summary: An upstairs lounge positioned beside academic resources in Anderson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Anderson Hall page places a student lounge, digital classroom, and education library on the building’s upper level.
cards.access_notes: The page confirms the lounge but publishes neither dedicated hours nor a drop-in reservation policy.

cards.title: Read Reflectively at Bonnier
cards.subtitle: An unscheduled-use space for meditation, prayer, and text study
cards.notes: Check that the center is unscheduled, then choose quiet reading or reflection; request the room separately for an organized gathering.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative room for focused reading when no program is scheduled.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus says community members may use the Bonnier Multifaith Center during unscheduled times and lists text studies and contemplative practices among its activities.
cards.access_notes: Informal use is limited to unscheduled times; organized uses require a space request.

cards.entity_name: Olin Hall physics lounge and library spaces
cards.title: Work Near the Physics Tools
cards.subtitle: Program-oriented lounge and library space with computers and equipment
cards.notes: Use this option if you belong to the physics program; confirm equipment permissions before building a session around specialized tools.
cards.short_summary: A discipline-focused environment combining seating, references, and technical access.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus documents dedicated physics lounge and library spaces in Olin Hall with access to computers and equipment for physics students.
cards.access_notes: These are physics-program spaces; the page does not establish general public access or equipment-reservation rules.

cards.title: Move a Project Off the Page
cards.subtitle: Design, building, and testing space for course and independent work
cards.notes: Confirm training and equipment access before arriving, then bring project work that genuinely needs a place to design, build, or test.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on alternative for assignments centered on making and testing.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Olin Hall page says fabrication spaces for designing, building, and testing projects are available for student use both in and outside class.
cards.access_notes: Student use is documented, but training, supervision, reservations, and individual equipment permissions are not specified.

cards.title: Settle Into Sohre’s Study Room
cards.subtitle: A dedicated study environment inside a residence hall
cards.notes: Choose this only if you have legitimate residence-hall access, and verify locally whether the room has scheduling or quiet-use expectations.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-labeled study room for residents and properly hosted guests.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus lists a dedicated study room among Sohre Hall’s amenities.
cards.access_notes: This is inside residential housing; the source does not publish room reservations, hours, or public-access rights.

cards.title: Handle Computer-Based Work in Sohre
cards.subtitle: A residence-hall computer room separate from the study room
cards.notes: Confirm resident access and software availability before relying on this room for an assignment, printing task, or specialized file format.
cards.short_summary: An in-hall option for coursework that requires a computer workstation.
cards.evidence_claim: Gustavus lists a computer room as a distinct Sohre Hall amenity alongside its lounge, kitchen, and study room.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall access applies; workstation count, software, printing, hours, and reservation rules are not published.

cards.entity_name: Saint Peter Public Library study rooms
cards.title: Ask for a Small Library Study Room
cards.subtitle: Two first-come rooms sized for two or three people
cards.notes: Go to library staff when you need the room unlocked; keep the group to three or fewer and have a backup because reservations are not accepted.
cards.short_summary: Small, nonreservable rooms for private study, calls, or compact groups.
cards.evidence_claim: The City documents two Saint Peter Public Library study rooms for two to three people, available first come rather than by reservation and unlocked on request.
cards.access_notes: Library operating hours apply; ask staff to unlock a room. Capacity is two to three people, and reservations are not accepted.

cards.entity_name: Minnesota Room at Saint Peter Public Library
cards.title: Reserve the Minnesota Room
cards.subtitle: A library room accommodating groups of up to six
cards.notes: Call the main library number or ask at the checkout desk before assembling your group, and keep attendance within the six-person capacity.
cards.short_summary: A reservable small-group room with more capacity than the drop-in rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the Saint Peter Public Library’s Minnesota Room holds up to six people and may be reserved by phone or at the checkout desk.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is available through the main library number or checkout desk; library hours and a six-person limit apply.

cards.entity_name: Saint Peter Public Library Meeting Room
cards.title: Plan an Educational Group Session
cards.subtitle: A reservable room for qualifying organizations and group activities
cards.notes: Use this for a qualifying educational group, not an informal solo session; arrange the reservation through the Recreation Office in advance.
cards.short_summary: A formal meeting option for organized educational or public-service work.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that the library meeting room is open to organizations or groups conducting educational, cultural, civic, or public-service activities, with reservations made through the Recreation Office.
cards.access_notes: Use is limited to qualifying group activities and requires a Recreation Office reservation; the cited page does not state a fee.
